source: A starting checklist for a first review, written for this application; edit to taste

rules.title: No governing law clause
rules.note: Without a governing law clause the applicable law is left to the courts to decide.

rules.title: Liability is uncapped for some breaches
rules.note: Check which breaches are carved out of the cap and whether insurance covers them.

rules.title: No cap on liability found
rules.note: A missing cap means each party is exposed to the full damages the law allows.

rules.title: No right to terminate without cause
rules.note: The parties may be bound for the whole term unless the other side breaches.

rules.title: Automatic renewal with a notice window
rules.note: Calendar the notice deadline; missing it renews the contract for another term.

rules.title: Renewal term without a stated notice period
rules.note: Check how and when the renewal can be stopped.

rules.title: Non-compete obligation
rules.note: Check the scope, the territory and the duration, and whether it survives termination.

rules.title: Exclusivity obligation
rules.note: Check which party is bound and for how long.

rules.title: Most favored nation pricing
rules.note: Pricing given to others may have to be matched.

rules.title: Change of control clause
rules.note: A sale or merger may give the other side a right to terminate or consent.

rules.title: Liquidated damages
rules.note: Check the amounts and whether they could be read as a penalty.

rules.title: Irrevocable or perpetual licence
rules.note: The licence may outlive the contract; check what it covers.

rules.title: Minimum commitment
rules.note: Check the amounts, the period and what happens on a shortfall.

rules.title: Assignment needs consent
rules.note: Relevant for a restructuring or a sale of the business.

rules.title: Audit rights
rules.note: Check who may audit, how often and at whose cost.

rules.title: No insurance obligation found
rules.note: Consider whether one side should carry cover for the risks of the deal.

rules.title: No dispute resolution clause detected
rules.note: Disputes go to the courts of whichever forum has jurisdiction.
